race_context: The 'Smith-Green School Board' seats belong to Smith-Green Community Schools, based in Churubusco, which serves Smith Township in Whitley County and Green Township in Noble County {nces_sg}{wc_sb_2024}{wiki_sg}. Federal data list 1,103 students in two schools in 2024-25 {nces_sg}. Dr. Paul Voigt is superintendent {sg_admin}.

The board has five members: three district seats (Districts 1 and 2 in Smith Township, District 3 in Green Township), elected in 2020, 2024 and 2028, and two at-large seats, elected in 2018, 2022 and 2026 {wc_sb_2024}. Every member is elected by voters in both townships {wc_sb_2024}. Under the county's filing guide, at-large members can live in any district, but the two at-large members cannot live in the same district {wc_sb_2024}.

Current members: Emily Putt (District 1), Brian Clark (District 2) and Jermiah Johnson (District 3), with terms to Dec. 31, 2028; and Kassie Taksey ('District 1 At Large') and Jeremy Hart ('District 2 At Large'), with terms ending Dec. 31, 2026 {sg_board}. Putt, Clark and Johnson were elected unopposed in 2024 {wc_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: both at-large seats, listed by Whitley County as 'Smith Green Community School Board – At Large (2)' {wc_2026_offices}. The state list shows the race as 'vote for 1' {in_list}; this guide could not confirm how the two seats appear on the ballot. Three candidates are running: incumbent Kassie Taksey and newcomers David Schafer and Marcus B Elam; incumbent Jeremy Hart is not on the ballot {in_list}{sg_board}.

2022 results (Whitley County portion only): Whitley County listed the races as Smith-Green 'SB District 1', 'District 2' and 'District 3' {wc_2022}. Kassie Jo Taksey won District 1 with 783 votes to 629 for Brice Lee Winget, and Jeremy A. Hart won District 2 with 907 votes to 440 for Steven Thomas {wc_2022}. Noble County's share of the vote was not checked.

Party labels: Schafer and Taksey are listed as Republicans and Elam as an Independent {in_list}. Candidates filed in the Whitley County Clerk's office from May 19 to noon June 18, 2026 {wc_2026_offices}.

Operating referendum on the same ballot (Nov. 3, 2026): the district asks voters to continue its operating referendum for up to eight years, changing the current maximum rate of $0.6280 to no more than $0.4988 per $100 of assessed value, with a maximum annual levy of $2,176,300 {dlgf_sg}. The ballot question says it responds to 'reductions in property tax revenue' and would fund health and safety, teacher and staff retention, class sizes, transportation and academic programs; it renews the referendum voters passed in 2018 {dlgf_sg}. The district's spending plan budgets about 52% ($1,131,676) for teachers, staff and class sizes and about 16% each for health and safety, transportation, and academic and support programs {sg_spending}.

Tax figures in the ballot question: it states that if the question is not approved, the tax bill on a median residence of $200,000 would decrease by $431 a year; the state's ruling separately records a county-certified increase of $566 for the median household if it passes {dlgf_sg}. The state approved the ballot language July 23, 2026 {dlgf_sg}. This guide found no news reporting on the referendum or on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district's budget.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the candidates' views. Board agendas and minutes are posted on the district's online meeting portal {sg_agendas}.
